images.title: First common multiple
images.purpose: Show that for the co-prime pair 3 and 5 the first common multiple is 3 × 5 = 15.
images.composition: One number line centred with lots of space, and one label below.
images.exact_structure: One horizontal number line with 16 evenly spaced ticks for 0 to 15. Above the line, 5 teal #0072B2 arcs for jumps of 3: 0 to 3, 3 to 6, 6 to 9, 9 to 12, 12 to 15. Below the line, 3 amber #E69F00 arcs for jumps of 5: 0 to 5, 5 to 10, 10 to 15. The tick at 15 is marked reddish purple #CC79A7. Below, centred: one equation. Exactly 1 line, 5 teal arcs, 3 amber arcs, 1 marked point.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
any arc ending off a tick or any tick that is unevenly spaced
images.takeaway: For co-prime numbers the first common multiple is their product.
images.description: Number line 0 to 15 with 5 teal jumps of 3 above and 3 amber jumps of 5 below, both meeting at 15.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to say where the two sets of jumps first meet.

image_decisions.why: One clean picture carries the main idea of this concept.
